page.layout: Printed page 382. Two parallel columns of worked examples (Examen primi exempli, left; Examen secundi exempli, right), with the result "5 6 4 3" below the right column. Below them, running text in one column, then a centred italic heading, then a paragraph with a drop cap. Catchword "Primus" at the lower right. Running head "DE ARITHMETICA." at the top right. Page number top left. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: Probatio Divisionis fit vere per mul-tiplicationem.
main_text.p: Quotum per Divisore multiplico. Quod vero in Divisione remansit, id directè sub-noto à dextra versus siniftram procedens. Deinde per additionem numeros colligo: Et si tum Dividendus producitur, semper bene numeratum est.
Hastenus quatuor numerationis species fuere traditæ: sequitur Aurea Regula.
main_text.head: Quid est Aurea Regula?
main_text.p: EST, qua ex trib. oblatis numeris, quartus producitur. Vulgò vocatur Regula Detri, seu Mercatorum.
Numerus primæ positionis notetur primo loco à siniftra progrediedo versus dextram, numerus secundæ positionis, secundo loco, numerus Quæstionis tertio po-natur loco.

page.notes: The printed "Hastenus" uses long s; transcribed as plain s. Printed spelling "progrediedo" and "(3" left as printed. The result "5 6 4 3" is set apart below the right-hand example and is transcribed as a separate line. Superscript-looking digits in "5 4 3 1 2" are read as ordinary digits.
